s12-v19.sanskrit_cite: aparimitarūpam ahaṃ taṃ taṃ bhāvaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ paśyan tvām eva viśvarūpaṃ nijanāthaṃ sādhu paśyeyam

s12-v20.plain_english: Why doesn't mind haunt what limbs love, the desired thing for desire? If no nature is harmed and my supreme wish is filled...
s12-v20.sanskrit_cite: bhavadaṅgagataṃ tam eva kasmān na manaḥ paryaṭatīṣṭam artham artham prakṛtikṣatir asti no tathāsya mama cecchā paripūryate paraiva

s12-v21.plain_english: Hundreds, they say, by Your power, with this very eye — even plough-walking — always see Your body ahead.
s12-v21.sanskrit_cite: śataśaḥ kila te tavānubhāvād bhagavan ke 'py amunaiva cakṣuṣā ye api hālikaceṣṭayā carantaḥ paripaśyanti bhavadvapuḥ sadāgre

s12-v22.plain_english: No thought rises unstained by Your will; always good or else — thus I roam as Yours on earth, feast of Your foot unstopped.
s12-v22.sanskrit_cite: na sā matir udeti yā na bhavati tvadicchāmayī sadā śubham athetarad bhagavataivam ācaryate ato 'smi bhavadātmako bhuvi yathā tathā sañcaran sthi to 'niśam abādhitatvadamalaṅghripūjotsavaḥ

s12-v23.plain_english: May insight rise well in Your deep sayings; then practiced power too, and unpausing worship-addiction.
s12-v23.sanskrit_cite: bhavadīyagabhīrabhāṣiteṣu pratibhā samyag udetu me puro 'taḥ tadanuṣṭhitaśaktir apy atas tadbhavadarcāvyasanaṃ ca nirvirāmam

s12-v24.plain_english: In dealings too, always, may this sense-heap appear to me as Your limb — not self-warranted.
s12-v24.sanskrit_cite: vyavahārapade 'pi sarvadā pratibhātv arthakalāpa eṣa mām bhavato 'vayavo yathā na tu svata evādaraṇīyatāṃ gataḥ

s12-v25.plain_english: Mind roaming freely in its fields, unswerving — may I ever be worship-skilled toward You.
s12-v25.sanskrit_cite: manasi svarasena yatra tatra pracaraty apy aham asya gocareṣu prasṛto 'py avilola eva yuṣmatparicaryācaturaḥ sadā bhaveyam

s12-v26.plain_english: Lord, by Your will alone Your slave I was made — another's no power here — yet why never see Your face-moon?
s12-v26.sanskrit_cite: bhagavan bhavadicchayaiva dāsas tava jāto 'smi parasya nātra śaktiḥ katham eṣa tathāpi vaktrabimbaṃ tava paśyāmi na jātu citram etat

s12-v27.plain_english: The eager toward You who face You as counter-form — ah, what would befall them, what practice would fruit for them?
s12-v27.sanskrit_cite: samutsukās tvāṃ prati ye bhavantaṃ pratyartharūpād avalokayanti teṣām aho kiṃ tadupasthitaṃ syāt kiṃ sādhanaṃ vā phalitaṃ bhavet tat

s12-v28.plain_english: May things be as things by Your being for me; thus may nothing be otherwise, nothing but You.
s12-v28.sanskrit_cite: bhāvā bhāvatayā santu bhavadbhāvena me bhava tathā na kiñcid apy astu na kiñcid bhavato 'nyathā

s12-v29.plain_english: May nothing-at-all be nothing, something-at-all be something to me; in all ways may You be worship-received.
s12-v29.sanskrit_cite: yan na kiñcid api tanna kiñcid apy astu kiñcid api kiñcid eva me sarvathā bhavatu tāvatā bhavān sarvato bhavati labdhapūjitaḥ

s13-v01.plain_english: In brief, Lord, hear how pleasure and pain stand for me: meeting You is pleasure; being parted from You, my Lord, is pain.
s13-v01.sanskrit_cite: saṃgrahena sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ māṃ prati sthitam idaṃ śṛṇu prabho saukhyam eṣa bhavatā samāgamaḥ svāminā viraha eva duḥkhitā

s13-v02.plain_english: Even the subtlest inward moment when You do not appear — wipe it out everywhere, Lord, and reveal Your own stainless form.
s13-v02.sanskrit_cite: antar apy atitarām aṇīyasī yā tvadaprathanakālikāsti me tām apīśa parimṛjya sarvataḥ svaṃ svarūpam amalaṃ prakāśaya

s13-v03.plain_english: Let me live or die or be anything else — if only I abide, always worshipping, in Your world-full body at undying consciousness-nectar time.
s13-v03.sanskrit_cite: tāvake vapuṣi viśvanirbhare citsudhārasamaye niratyaye tiṣṭhataḥ satatam arcataḥ prabhuṃ jīvitaṃ mṛtam athānyad astu me

s13-v04.plain_english: "I am the Lord, I alone am formed, learned, fortunate — who else is parallel to me in the world?" Such pride shines supreme in Your lovers.
s13-v04.sanskrit_cite: īśvaro 'ham aham eva rūpavān paṇḍito 'smi subhago 'smi ko 'paraḥ matsamo 'sti jagatīti śobhate mānitā tvadanurāgiṇaḥ param

s13-v05.plain_english: By the awareness of things exactly as they stand, make me fit for worshipping Your feet — me, born of telling non-duality's nectar that swallows renown.
s13-v05.sanskrit_cite: devadeva bhavadadvayāmṛtākhyātisaṃharaṇalabdhajanmanā tad yathāsthitapadārthasaṃvidā māṃ kuruṣva caraṇārcanocitam

s13-v06.plain_english: Meditated upon, then seen, then the Lord Himself is touched. May this worship-festival of Yours be always mine, by Your power.
s13-v06.sanskrit_cite: dhyāyate tad anu dṛśyate tataḥ spṛśyate ca parameśvaraḥ svayam yatra pūjanamahotsavaḥ sa me sarvadāstu bhavato 'nubhāvataḥ

s13-v07.plain_english: Seeing things as they stand, and Your worship-festival — this pair grounds each other, expanding always among devotees.
s13-v07.sanskrit_cite: yady athāsthitapadārthadarśanaṃ yuṣmadarcanamahotsavaś ca yaḥ yugmam etad itaretarāśrayaṃ bhaktiśāliṣu sadā vijṛmbhate

s13-v08.plain_english: Through every sense-door, constantly, may I drink the wine of Your worship-rasa in all-filled feeling-cups — and be mad.
s13-v08.sanskrit_cite: tattadindriyamukhena santataṃ yuṣmadarcanarasāyanāsavam sarvabhāvacaṣakeṣu pūriteṣv āpibann api bhaveyam unmadaḥ

s13-v09.plain_english: Where not an atom is felt as other, and all expands self-shining — there, Lord, keep me standing, Your constant worshipper, in Your city.
s13-v09.sanskrit_cite: anyavedyam aṇumātram asti na svaprakāśam akhilaṃ vijṛmbhate yatra nātha bhavataḥ pure sthitaṃ tatra me kuru sadā tavārcituḥ

s13-v10.plain_english: Though You posted even me to slaves' quarters by Your own will — am I not fit by seeing, even by foot-massage?
s13-v10.sanskrit_cite: dāsadhāmni viniyojito 'py ahaṃ svecchayaiva parameśvara tvayā darśanena na kim asmi pātritaḥ pādasaṃvahanakarmaṇāpi vā

s13-v11.plain_english: At the moment of grace's descent You never deliberate, Lord, never — so what has come over You now, delaying the rite of Your self-revelation to me?
s13-v11.sanskrit_cite: śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit adya māṃ prati kim āgataṃ yataḥ svaprakāśanavidhau vilambase

s13-v12.plain_english: In each object shining outside, and inside joined with the Goddess, may I always behold You, world-full — worshipped by my own hands.
s13-v12.sanskrit_cite: tatra tatra viṣaye bahirvibhāty antare ca parameśvarīyutam tvāṃ jagattritayanirbharaṃ sadā lokayeya nijapāṇipūjitam

s13-v13.plain_english: May I always mount the Master's palace, unobstructed, by mere resolve — bliss-freed in the play of drinking supreme-nectar-wine.
s13-v13.sanskrit_cite: svāmisaudham abhisandhimātrato nirvibandham adhiruhya sarvadā syāṃ prasāda paramāmṛtāsavāpānakeliparilabdhanirvṛtiḥ

s13-v14.plain_english: Whatever wonder arises in all fair things by mere touch — by that the unwavering worship Your body.
s13-v14.sanskrit_cite: yatsamastasubhagārthavastuṣu sparśamātravidhinā camatkṛtim tāṃ samarpayati tena te vapuḥ pūjayanty acalabhaktiśālinaḥ

s13-v15.plain_english: Swelling all by Thyself, shining — You touch the universe, touching form; whatever whirls by its own juice — that is the swelling world.
s13-v15.sanskrit_cite: sphārayasy akhilam ātmanā sphuran viśvam āmṛśasi rūpam āmṛśan yat svayaṃ nijarasena ghurṇase tat samullasati bhāvamaṇḍalam

s13-v16.plain_english: Who sees this whole object-circle without construction as Your body, Lord — the world filled with his own self's side — for him, ever-happy, whence fear?
s13-v16.sanskrit_cite: yo 'vikalpam idam arthamaṇḍalaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagaty asya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam

s13-v17.plain_english: The kālakūṭa poison set in Your throat's corner is great nectar to me; even taken nectar, if difference prevails, does not please me.
s13-v17.sanskrit_cite: kaṇṭhakoṇaviniviṣṭam īśa te kālakūṭam api me mahāmṛtam apy upāttam amṛtaṃ bhavadvapur bhedavṛtti yadi rocate na me

s13-v18.plain_english: Graced with song-mouths lovely with prattling of You, may I be — my heart forever gone to what Your worship-loving prefers.
s13-v18.sanskrit_cite: tvatpralāpamayaraktagītikāni tya yuktavadanopaśobhitaḥ syām athāpi bhavadarcanakriyāpreyasīparigatāśayaḥ sadā

s13-v19.plain_english: Alas, the Supreme's play cannot be counted — and so the nectar-full body He gave me, He does not let me drink — so it is.
s13-v19.sanskrit_cite: īhitaṃ na bata pārameśvaraṃ śakyate gaṇayituṃ tathā ca me dattam apy amṛtanirbharaṃ vapuḥ svaṃ na pātum anumanyate tathā

s13-v20.plain_english: Entering You — fathomless, construction-free, non-dual, devourer of all things' meaning — O Umā's Lord, may I always worship and praise.
s13-v20.sanskrit_cite: tvām agādham avikalpam advayaṃ svaṃ svarūpam akhilārthaghasmaram āviśann aham umeśa sarvadā pūjayeyam abhisaṃstuvīya ca

s14-v01.plain_english: Before my own master, treasure of victory-fortune — may I taste for a moment the nectar of victory-proclamation.
s14-v01.sanskrit_cite: jayalakṣmīnidhānasya nijasya svāminaḥ puraḥ jayodghoṣaṇapīyūṣarasam āsvādaye kṣaṇam

s14-v02.plain_english: Victory: one Rudra, one Śiva, great god, great Lord — Pārvatī's lover, Śarva, eldest of all gods.
s14-v02.sanskrit_cite: jayaikarudraikaśiva mahādeva maheśvara pārvatīpraṇayiñ śarva sarvagīrvāṇapūrvaja

s14-v03.plain_english: Victory: brow-eyed sole mark of the three-worlds' Lord; victory: poison-mark-throated, who drank the black poison for the worlds' pain.

s14-v04.plain_english: Victory: whose self is the embodied three powers, hundred-spike-bright-handed; victory: whose lotus-feet are worshipped, wishes accomplished by mere will.

s14-v05.plain_english: Victory: bearer of a body beyond worlds, streaming a hundred beauties; victory: single-braided, of unwasting Ganges, ash-seized.

s14-v06.plain_english: Victory: smeared with milk-ocean-spread moonlight shade; victory: snow-ornamented, jewel-beloved, risen from the Lord's limb-contact.

s14-v07.plain_english: Victory: refuge like the one undying cool-rayed digit; victory: consecrated by ever-moist Ganges and universal lordship.

s14-v08.plain_english: Victory: whose lowest-limb-touch purifies cowherds; victory: fixed-present where intoxicated devotees gather.

s14-v09.plain_english: Victory: who dupes the childish, showing a hot place of His own will; victory: fit vessel for Gauri-embrace-fortune.

s14-v10.plain_english: Victory: greedy for love-gifts wet with devotion-rasa; victory: pleased by the speech-dance of devotees drunk with devotion.

s14-v11.plain_english: Victory: whose rise-and-fall is the power of Brahmā-and-first-gods; victory: whose command world-lord-rows bear on heads.

s14-v12.plain_english: Victory: whose manifest glory is His seal set on all worlds; victory: great Lord of all, down to giving the very self.

s14-v13.plain_english: Victory: secondless at the creation-wish moment; victory: with sole Goddess-helper bearing lordship's burden.

s14-v14.plain_english: Victory: who seized all three worlds in one stride; victory: unbroken Lord-sound sung from childhood.

s14-v15.plain_english: Victory: innately high, needing no pity and the rest; victory: Bhairava before whom great Death is made.

s14-v16.plain_english: Victory: unopposed in fierce world-ending acts; victory: hundredfold-good-named recitation-following.

s14-v17.plain_english: Victory: nectar-mine-ocean poured out in play; victory: whose instant anger dries the world-ending in a flash.

s14-v18.plain_english: Victory: sole lamp of beings blind in delusion-darkness; victory: wakeful supreme Person while the sleeping world...

s14-v19.plain_english: Victory: life-of-life humming inside the body-mountain cave; victory: best rasa sporting in good minds' sky.

s14-v20.plain_english: Victory: mountain-lord born of high gold-ore; victory: moon rising as calamity-portent over the wicked.

s14-v21.plain_english: Victory: hard to reach by austerity-tormented sages and gods; victory: seen by the world of devotion-madmen mounted on every state.

s14-v22.plain_english: Victory: who leafed His dependents spreading His own wealth; victory: whose sole purpose is fondling surrendered people.

s14-v23.plain_english: Victory: sole performer of creating-staying-destroying; victory: festival of the play-lotus blooming in drunken devotion.

s14-v24.plain_english: Victory, worthy of victory! Victory, conqueror of birth, aging, dying! Victory, eldest of worlds... victory, victory... O three-eyed One.
s14-v24.sanskrit_cite: jaya jayabhājana jaya jitajanmajarāmaraṇa jaya jagajjyeṣṭha jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya jaya tryakṣa

s15-v01.plain_english: Stain-washing books exist, and their crossers too — yogins, scholars stand healthy — but devotees alone, in truth.
s15-v01.sanskrit_cite: trimalakṣālino granthāḥ santi tatpāragāstathā yoginaḥ paṇḍitāḥ svasthās tvadbhaktā eva tattvataḥ

s15-v02.plain_english: Māyā-time-limit-passion and the rest as food, fully fed — devotees stroll happy, Lord, on the world's shore.
s15-v02.sanskrit_cite: māyīyakālaniyatirāgādyāhāratarpitāḥ caranti sukhino nātha bhaktimanto jagattaṭe

s15-v03.plain_english: Laughing or crying, they babble You aloud — devotees, whose praise-word offerings are ornaments apart.
s15-v03.sanskrit_cite: rudanto vā hasanto vā tvām uccaiḥ pralapanty amī bhaktāḥ stutipadoccāropacārāḥ pṛthag eva te

s15-v04.plain_english: Not detached, not master, not liberation-desiring is Your worshipper — but drunk with soaring devotion-liquor-rasa.
s15-v04.sanskrit_cite: na virakto na cāpīśo mokṣākāṅkṣī tvadarcakaḥ bhaveyam api tūdriktabhaktyāsavarasonmadaḥ

s15-v05.plain_english: Who worships by drawing the outer inside the heart alone — to him, in devotion-nectar floods, I bow.
s15-v05.sanskrit_cite: bāhyaṃ hṛdaya evāntar abhihṛtyaiva yo 'rcati tvām īśa bhaktipīyūṣarasapūrair namāmi tam

s15-v06.plain_english: Between dharma and adharma acts, knowledges, pleasure and pain selves — devotees taste SOMETHING — ah!
s15-v06.sanskrit_cite: dharmādharmātmanor antaḥ kriyayor jñānayos tathā sukhaduḥkhātmanor bhaktāḥ kim apy āsvādayanty aho

s15-v07.plain_english: Blind ones, lepers even — they shine, supreme, ornamented by blazing devotion to You.
s15-v07.sanskrit_cite: carācarapitaḥ svāmin apy andhā api kuṣṭhinaḥ śobhante param uddāmabhavadbhaktivibhūṣaṇāḥ

s15-v08.plain_english: Gleaners, winnowers, enemies' shadows even — yet by devotion's heat they rule even the king of kings.
s15-v08.sanskrit_cite: śiloñchapicchakaśipuvicchāyāṅgā api prabho bhavadbhaktimahoṣmaṇo rājarājam apīśate

s15-v09.plain_english: Though rolling in nectar-wet devotion, yet wanting to climb — some worship You with mind alone, standing all around.
s15-v09.sanskrit_cite: sudhārdrāyāṃ bhavadbhaktau luṭhatāpy ārurukṣuṇā cetasaiva vibho 'rcanti kecit tvām abhitaḥ sthitāḥ

s15-v10.plain_english: To be guarded, grown, honored, Lord — this great wealth of devotion that ends bad rebirths.
s15-v10.sanskrit_cite: rakṣaṇīyaṃ vardhanīyaṃ bahumānyam idaṃ prabho saṃsāradurgatiharaṃ bhavadbhaktimahādhanam

s15-v11.plain_english: Lord, though Your devotees love You — abandoning jealousy toward Her, may She always be pleased, the Mistress.
s15-v11.sanskrit_cite: nātha te bhaktajanatā yady api tvayi rāgiṇī tathāpīrṣyāṃ vihāyāsyās tuṣṭāstu svāminī sadā

s15-v12.plain_english: Your future being first; when devotion's occasion comes and the milk-ocean is churned — curd-greed is killed.
s15-v12.sanskrit_cite: bhavadbhāvaḥ puro bhāvī prāpte tvadbhaktisambhave labdhe dugdhamahākumbhe hatā dadhani gṛdhnutā

s15-v13.plain_english: Is this not attainment beyond compare — ever-growing devotion to Śambhu, always new? What happiness does it not stream?
s15-v13.sanskrit_cite: kim iyaṃ na siddhir atulā kiṃ vā mukhyaṃ na saukhyam āsravati bhaktir upacīyamānā yeyaṃ śambhoḥ sadātanī bhavati

s15-v14.plain_english: Sunk in my dirty mind, Your devotion gem-creeper — alas — does not spread its own superhuman wealth-blossomings.
s15-v14.sanskrit_cite: manasi maline madīyemagnā tvadbhaktimaṇilatā kaṣṭam na nijān api tanute tānapauruṣeyān svasampadullāsān

s15-v15.plain_english: Devotion to the Lord of three worlds IS supreme attainment — but lacking supernormal powers, is it not full? — that is my worry.
s15-v15.sanskrit_cite: bhaktir bhagavati bhavati trilokanāthe nanūttamā siddhiḥ kiṃ tv aṇimādikavirahāt saiva na pūrṇeti cintā me

s15-v16.plain_english: Outside and in, the fragrance of Your praise-blossoms' opening perfumes even hostile ascetics dwelling near.
s15-v16.sanskrit_cite: bāhyato 'ntar api cotkaṭonmiṣattryambakastavakasaurabhāḥ śubhāḥ vāsayanty api viruddhavāsanān yogino nikaṭavāsino 'khilān

s15-v17.plain_english: By no account is there any light; the whole world fast asleep — yet at Your Śivarātri post, devotees always worship You.
s15-v17.sanskrit_cite: jyotir asti kathayāpi na kiṃ cid viśvam apy atisuṣuptam aśeṣam yatra nātha śivarātripade 'smin nityam arcayati bhaktajanas tvām

s15-v18.plain_english: Let goodness expand in true worship of gracious Śiva; let Śaṅkara-foot-dust heaps sport on the crown — to cut even passion-memories, let darkness swell, or the triple world dissolve in Your self-loss.
s15-v18.sanskrit_cite: sattvaṃ satyaguṇe śive bhagavati sphārībhavatv arcane cūḍāyāṃ vilasantu śaṅkarapadaprodyadrajaḥsaṅcayāḥ rāgādismṛtivāsanām api samucchettuṃ tamo jṛmbhatāṃ śambho me bhavatāt tvadātmavilaye traiguṇyavargo 'thavā

s15-v19.plain_english: The world-road is long; limbs burnt by harsh diseases; pleasures unenjoyed; happiness never long — thus I have become useless, moon-crest-foot-pressed, wholly Yours — so make me, quickly, long-and-rich in great fortune, as Your devotee.
s15-v19.sanskrit_cite: saṃsārādhvā sudūraḥ kharataravividhavyādhidagdhāṅgayaṣṭiḥ bhogā naivopabhuktā yad api sukham abhūj jātu nanno cirāya itthaṃ vyartho 'smi jātaḥ śaśidharacaraṇākrāntikāntottamāṅgas tvadbhaktaś ceti tan me kuru sapadi mahāsampado dīrghadīrghāḥ

s16-v01.plain_english: Nothing blocks folk, nothing blocks devotees from Your veiling.
s16-v01.sanskrit_cite: na kiñcid eva lokānāṃ bhavadāvaraṇaṃ prati \var{yat kiṃ cid eva bhūtānāṃ\em \cit \Naresvaraparīksā} na kiñcid eva bhaktānāṃ bhavadāvaraṇaṃ prati

s16-v02.plain_english: Though reached by method-ladders, crowded with attributes — to devotees the self appears at once, pure.
s16-v02.sanskrit_cite: apy upāyakramaprāpyaḥ saṅkulo 'pi viśeṣaṇaiḥ bhaktibhājāṃ bhavān ātmā sakṛc chuddho 'vabhāsate

s16-v03.plain_english: Laughing victors, laughing conquered — drunk on His devotion-nectar, whoever they are, Lord.
s16-v03.sanskrit_cite: jayanto 'pi hasanty ete jitā api hasanti ca bhavadbhaktisudhāpānamattāḥ ke 'py eva ye prabho

s16-v04.plain_english: May I never dry up, never seek release — full of His devotion-rasa, best-liked, attained.
s16-v04.sanskrit_cite: śuṣkakaṃ maiva siddheya maiva mucyeya vāpi tu svādiṣṭhaparakāṣṭāptatvadbhaktirasanirbharaḥ

s16-v05.plain_english: As unknown before was this devotion-rasa of Yours to me — so, Lord, may that same one grow.
s16-v05.sanskrit_cite: yathaivajñātapūrvo 'yaṃ bhavadbhaktiraso mama ghaṭitas tadvad īśāna sa eva paripuṣyatu

s16-v06.plain_english: Truly, Lord, I have no other prayer-course — only may such immersion-possession by devotion be mine always.
s16-v06.sanskrit_cite: satyena bhagavan nānyaḥ prārthanāprasaro 'sti me kevalaṃ sa tathā ko 'pi bhaktyāveśo 'stu me sadā

s16-v07.plain_english: Drunk on devotion I may rage, repent, leap, shout "Śiva" — enough.
s16-v07.sanskrit_cite: bhaktikṣīvo 'pi kupyeyaṃ bhavāyānuśayīya ca tathā haseyaṃ udyāṃ ca raṭeyaṃ ca śivety alam

s16-v08.plain_english: In crisis or at peace, weeping or laughing, deep or distracted — may I be, Lord, by devotion.
s16-v08.sanskrit_cite: viṣamastho 'pi svastho 'pi rudann api hasann api gambhīro 'pi vicitto 'pi bhaveyaṃ bhaktitaḥ prabho

s16-v09.plain_english: For devotees nothing to be known, inside You or out — where consciousness-natured You stand thought-free.
s16-v09.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānāṃ nāsti saṃvedyaṃ tvadantar yadi vā bahiḥ ciddharmā yatra na bhavān nirvikalpaḥ sthitaḥ svayam

s16-v10.plain_english: Devotees rejoice even at abusers — pierced within, bristling with sharp horripilation, as if by nectar-drops.
s16-v10.sanskrit_cite: bhaktā nindānukare 'pi tavāmṛtakaṇair iva hṛṣyanty evāntarāviddhās tīkṣṇaromāñcasūcibhiḥ

s16-v11.plain_english: Even pain-feeling ripens to enjoyment for devotees, whose all-awareness, moon-wet, is moonlight-made.
s16-v11.sanskrit_cite: duḥkhāpi vedanā bhaktimatāṃ bhogāya kalpate yeṣāṃ sudhārdrā sarvaiva saṃvit tvaccandrikāmayī

s16-v12.plain_english: Wherever held, devotees — inside and out — unfeigned, Your body-touch-taste-joy the same.
s16-v12.sanskrit_cite: yatra tatroparuddhānāṃ bhaktānāṃ bahirantare nirvyājaṃ tvadvapuḥsparśarasāsvādasukhaṃ samam

s16-v13.plain_english: In worship of Thy devotion, wiping out wretchedness's share that rests on duality — some taste the clear nectar-body.
s16-v13.sanskrit_cite: taveśa bhakter arcāyāṃ dainyāṃśaṃ dvayasaṃśrayam vilupyāsvādayanty eke vapur acchaṃ sudhāmayam

s16-v14.plain_english: Erring are pilgrim-eyes, divided — for division is just erring; but matchless, strifeless Being shines for devotees.
s16-v14.sanskrit_cite: bhrāntās tīrthadṛśo bhinnā bhrānter eva hi bhinnatā niṣpratidvandvi vastv ekaṃ bhaktānāṃ tvaṃ tu rājase

s16-v15.plain_english: Mind ripened past honor, contempt, love and the rest into stainlessness — how could its bearer be world-mannered?
s16-v15.sanskrit_cite: mānāvamānarāgādiniṣpākavimalaṃ manaḥ yasyāsau bhaktimāṃl lokatulyaśīlaḥ kathaṃ bhavet

s16-v16.plain_english: Passion-aversion-darkness conquered by devotion-light — who are the knowledge-rich before them?
s16-v16.sanskrit_cite: rāgadveṣandhakāro 'pi yeṣāṃ bhaktitviṣā jitaḥ teṣāṃ mahīyasām agre katame jñānaśālinaḥ

s16-v17.plain_english: Whose rite is devotion-nectar-drink-and-bath — high joy from beginning through end.

s16-v18.plain_english: Praised, sought, worshipped — for that alone devotees' world-life is praiseworthy.
s16-v18.sanskrit_cite: kīrtyaś cintāpadaṃ mṛgyaḥ pūjyo yena tvam eva tat bhavadbhaktimatāṃ ślāghyā lokayātrā bhavanmayī

s16-v19.plain_english: Liberation's name is but Your ripe devotion — mounted on its first stage, we are near-free.
s16-v19.sanskrit_cite: muktisaṃjñā vipakvāyā bhakter eva tvayi prabho tasyām ādyadaśārūḍhā muktakalpā vayaṃ tataḥ

s16-v20.plain_english: May pain's coming be great for me, self filled with devotion to Thee — may even pleasure's succession not turn from Thee.
s16-v20.sanskrit_cite: duḥkhāgamo 'pi bhūyān me tvadbhaktibharitātmanaḥ tvatparācī vibho mā bhūd api saukhyaparamparā

s16-v21.plain_english: You are pleased by devotion; devotion, You pleased — this mutual dependence is fitting, as You alone know.
s16-v21.sanskrit_cite: tvaṃ bhaktyā prīyase bhaktiḥ prīte tvayi ca nātha yat tadanyonyāśrayaṃ yuktaṃ yathā vettha tvam eva tat

s16-v22.plain_english: With form or formless, inside or out — to devotion-selves, always nectar, Lord.
s16-v22.sanskrit_cite: sākāro vā nirākaro vāntar vā bahir eva vā bhaktimattātmanāṃ nātha sarvathāsi sudhāmayaḥ

s16-v23.plain_english: In this very world, for Your devotees, another world-stand exists — fruit of joy-showing.
s16-v23.sanskrit_cite: asminn eva jagaty antar bhavadbhaktimataḥ prati harṣaprakāśanaphalam anyad eva jagatsthitam

s16-v24.plain_english: Devotion hidden, devotion supreme, devotion to the world-great Lord — devotion, ah, something in You, Śiva.
s16-v24.sanskrit_cite: guhye bhaktiḥ pare bhaktir bhaktir viśvamaheśvare tvayi śambhau śive deva bhaktir nāma kim apy aho

s16-v25.plain_english: Devotion, devotion, supreme devotion — I cry loud: let fierce devotion be mine supreme.
s16-v25.sanskrit_cite: bhaktir bhaktiḥ pare bhaktir bhaktir nāma samutkaṭā tāraṃ viraumi yat tīvrā bhaktir me 'stu paraṃ tvayi

s16-v26.plain_english: Since I am the birth-ground of all beauties — stuck to You, jewel or straw becomes priceless.
s16-v26.sanskrit_cite: yato 'smi sarvaśobhānāṃ prasavāvanir īśa tat tvayi lagnam anarghaṃ syād ratnam vā yadi vā tṛṇam

s16-v27.plain_english: From knower and from knowable, on whose knowing-road there is no parting from You — they win, Your devotees, ever fearless.
s16-v27.sanskrit_cite: āvedakād ā ca vedyād yeṣāṃ saṃvedanādhvani bhavatā na viyogo 'sti te jayanti bhavajjuṣaḥ

s16-v28.plain_english: Outside saṃsāra's hall, by some Thou art embraced — Lord, by others in that very place, self-tormenting, unreined.
s16-v28.sanskrit_cite: saṃsārasadaso bāhye kaiś cittvaṃ parirabhyase svāmin parais tu tatraiva tāmyadbhis tyaktayantraṇaiḥ

s16-v29.plain_english: With Śivā who eats, decks, celebrates the world, festival-hurried — hug tight, Śiva, I bow.
s16-v29.sanskrit_cite: pānāśanaprasādhanasambhuktasamastaviśvayā śivayā pralayotsavasarabhasayā dṛḍham upagūḍhaṃ śivaṃ vande

s16-v30.plain_english: Peerless overlordship wins, world-Lord, being subject-free — and so does Your otherness, by which this world shines as it does not.
s16-v30.sanskrit_cite: parameśvaratā jayaty apūrvā tava viśveśa yadīśitavyaśūnyā aparāpi tathaiva te yayedaṃ jagad ābhāti yathā tathā na bhāti

s17-v01.plain_english: Ah, this wins — sweet, this festival of worship — since tears give nectar-taste amply.
s17-v01.sanskrit_cite: aho ko 'pi jayaty eṣa svāduḥ pūjāmahotsavaḥ yato 'mṛtarasāsvādam aśrūṇy api dadaty alam

s17-v02.plain_english: All acts with His worship vanguard are successes; devotees made of Him are themselves successes.
s17-v02.sanskrit_cite: vyāpārāḥ siddhidāḥ sarve ye tvatpūjāpuraḥsarāḥ bhaktānāṃ tvanmayāḥ sarve svayaṃ siddhaya eva te

s17-v03.plain_english: In all beings, all states, at once, all-formed — worshipping You unceasing, they are my gods.
s17-v03.sanskrit_cite: sarvadā sarvabhāveṣu yugapat sarvarūpiṇam tvām arcayanty aviśrantaṃ ye mamaite 'dhidevatāḥ

s17-v04.plain_english: Meditation-perfected touch-festival of You — thus famed as worship-rule — be mine always.
s17-v04.sanskrit_cite: dhyānāyasatiraskārasiddhas tvatsparśanotsavaḥ pūjāvidhir iti khyāto bhaktānāṃ sa sadās tu me

s17-v05.plain_english: Equanimity-essence equinox-moment of devotees is always — ever-worshipping with Your being-rasa-nectar.

s17-v06.plain_english: Whose beginning and end are not, nor time-order — that deed is Yours, and its doers resort only to You.
s17-v06.sanskrit_cite: yasyānārambhaparyantau na ca kālakramaḥ prabho pūjātmāsau kriyā tasyāḥ kartāras tvajjuṣaḥ param

s17-v07.plain_english: Brahmā and the rest are fortunate, lords — in whose dream, even delusion, stands Your worship-festival.
s17-v07.sanskrit_cite: brahmādīnām apīśāste te ca saubhāgyabhāginaḥ yeṣāṃ svapne 'pi mohe 'pi sthitas tvatpūjanotsavaḥ

s17-v08.plain_english: Chanting, offering, bathing, meditating — and not only: ah, devotees' worshipping You — whenever, whatever, however much.
s17-v08.sanskrit_cite: japatāṃ juhvatāṃ snātāṃ dhyāyatāṃ na ca kevalam bhaktānāṃ bhavadabhyarcāmaho yāvad yadā tadā

s17-v09.plain_english: Tasting Your worship-nectar-joy, enjoying — to Indra and the rest, to Brahmā-chiefs: is anyone equal?
s17-v09.sanskrit_cite: bhavatpūjāsudhāsvādasambhogasukhinaḥ sadā indrādīnām atha brahmamukhyānām asti kaḥ samaḥ

s17-v10.plain_english: World-shaking, one-cause festival — what is got thereby, only devotees know who get it.
s17-v10.sanskrit_cite: jagatkṣobhaikajanake bhavatpūjāmahotsave yatprāpyaṃ prāpyate kiṃcid bhaktā eva vidanti tat

s17-v11.plain_english: Standing in Your abode, consciousness-formed, with body-speech-mind acts of all 36 principles — I always worship You, Lord.
s17-v11.sanskrit_cite: tvaddhāmni cinmaye sthitvā ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakarmabhiḥ kāyavākcittaceṣṭādyair arcaye tvāṃ sadā vibho

s17-v12.plain_english: Of me, enjoying union with Your worship — may all time pass, even endless: this I pray.
s17-v12.sanskrit_cite: bhavatpūjāmayāsaṅgasambhogasukhino mama prayātu kālaḥ sakalo 'py ananto 'pīyadarthaye

s17-v13.plain_english: Greedy for Your worship-enjoyment-nectar — may it grow daily for me and fruit always.
s17-v13.sanskrit_cite: bhavatpūjāmṛtarasābhogalampaṭata vibho vivardhatām anudinaṃ sadā ca phalatāṃ mama

s17-v14.plain_english: In Your ocean, nectar-one-rasa-full, worshipping You, great self, may I always sit.
s17-v14.sanskrit_cite: jagadvilayasañjātasudhaikarasanirbhare tvadabdhau tvāṃ mahātmānam arcannāsīya sarvadā

s17-v15.plain_english: Mind offered as sweet in Your rite — knots ever cut simply.
s17-v15.sanskrit_cite: aśeṣavāsanāgranthivicchedasaralaṃ sadā mano nivedyate bhaktaiḥ svādu pūjāvidhau tava

s17-v16.plain_english: Having taken stand on objects — these sense-courses of devotees — send them for Your worship-nectar-wine.
s17-v16.sanskrit_cite: adhiṣṭhāyaiva viṣayānimāḥ karaṇavṛttayaḥ bhaktānāṃ preṣayanti svatpūjārtham amṛtāsavam

s17-v17.plain_english: Agitated by devotion-heat, self-mastered — what else could liberate but drowning in worship of You?
s17-v17.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānāṃ bhaktisaṃvegamahoṣmavivaśātmanām ko 'nyo nirvāṇahetuḥ syāt tvatpūjāmṛtamajjanāt

s17-v18.plain_english: Perpetual foot-worship-nectar-drinking festival — may it be my sole grace-getting cause, Lord.
s17-v18.sanskrit_cite: satataṃ tvatpadābhyarcāsudhāpānamahotsavaḥ tvatprasādaikasamprāptihetur me nātha kalpatām

s17-v19.plain_english: Experiencing, Lord, moment by moment — Your worship-nectar-drinking-madness-joy-great-joy.

s17-v20.plain_english: Seen is the point of devotees' great worship-undertaking: that they taste impossible joy then.
s17-v20.sanskrit_cite: dṛṣṭartha eva bhaktānāṃ bhavatpūjāmahodyamaḥ tadaiva yad asambhāvyaṃ sukham āsvādayanti te

s17-v21.plain_english: Till Your worship-nectar-taste-festival is got, I count no drop of fortune's happiness tasted.
s17-v21.sanskrit_cite: yāvan na labdhas tvatpūjāsudhāsvādamahotsavaḥ tāvan nāsvādito manye lavo 'pi sukhasampadaḥ

s17-v22.plain_english: Without sense-seeking strain, Your abode's abiding is born in devotees — no getting needed, only madness with worship.
s17-v22.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānāṃ viṣayanveṣābhāsāyāsād vinaiva sā ayatnasiddhaṃ tvaddhāmasthitiḥ pūjāsu jāyate

s17-v23.plain_english: Nothing ungettable for devotees, nothing hard — they only roam, mad with worship.
s17-v23.sanskrit_cite: na prāpyam asti bhaktanāṃ nāpy eṣām asti durlabham kevalaṃ vicaranty ete bhavatpūjāmadonmadāḥ

s17-v24.plain_english: Ah, the devotees' heart-heavy worship-rule: praised, unmarked by begging.
s17-v24.sanskrit_cite: aho bhaktibharodāracetasāṃ varada tvayi slāghyaḥ pūjāvidhiḥ ko 'pi yo na yācñākalaṃkitaḥ

s17-v25.plain_english: What beauty is not, what joy not, what fortune not, what liberation not — this Mahādeva, since He is worshipped.
s17-v25.sanskrit_cite: kā na śobhā na ko hlādaḥ kā samṛddhir na vāparā ko vā na mokṣaḥ ko 'py eṣa mahādevo yad arcyate

s17-v26.plain_english: Nourished within by welling bright devotion-nectar — may this body be for Thy worship's use, always devoted.
s17-v26.sanskrit_cite: antarullasadacchācchabhaktipīyūṣapoṣitam bhavatpūjopayogāya śarīram idam astu me

s17-v27.plain_english: Dependent on Your foot-worship-enjoyment — may I, O world-Lord, be the one self-willed in movement.
s17-v27.sanskrit_cite: tvatpādapūjāsambhogaparatantraḥ sadā vibho bhūyāsaṃ jagatām īśa ekaḥ svacchandaceṣṭitaḥ

s17-v28.plain_english: To quench vision-touch-thirst for You — arises the cool, sweet great lake of Your worship.
s17-v28.sanskrit_cite: tvaddhyānadarśanasparśatṛṣi keṣām api prabho jāyate śītalasvādu bhavatpūjāmahāsaraḥ

s17-v29.plain_english: As You alone are the world's worship-enjoyment-vessel — so, Lord, is the devotee a vessel of worship-enjoyment.
s17-v29.sanskrit_cite: yathā tvam eva jagataḥ pūjāsambhogabhājanam tatheśa bhaktimān eva pūjāsambhogabhājanam

s17-v30.plain_english: Victor, Your festival — even the 36 agitated by it — great day.
s17-v30.sanskrit_cite: ko 'py asau jayati svāmin bhavatpūjāmahotsavaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśato 'pi tattvānāṃ kṣobho yatrollasaty alam

s17-v31.plain_english: Bow to those whose worship-things are themselves worshipped, by devotion-nectar-water.
s17-v31.sanskrit_cite: namas tebhyo vibho yeṣāṃ bhaktipīyūṣavāriṇā pūjyāny eva bhavanti tvatpūjopakaraṇāny api

s17-v32.plain_english: At worship's start, meditating mantra-placed His selfhood — devotees rest in supreme self, nowhere roaming.
s17-v32.sanskrit_cite: pūjārambhe vibho dhyātvā mantrādheyāṃ tvadātmatām svātmany eva pare bhaktā mānti harṣeṇa na kvacit

s17-v33.plain_english: Kingdoms blooming, world shared out in nectar-wine by festival-goers.
s17-v33.sanskrit_cite: rājyalābhādivotphullaiḥ kaiś cit pūjāmahotsave sudhāsavena sakalā jagatī saṃvibhajyate

s17-v34.plain_english: Whose moment-drink is worship-nectar — are they gods, freed, or whatever people?
s17-v34.sanskrit_cite: pūjāmṛtāpānamayo yeṣāṃ bhogaḥ pratikṣaṇam kiṃ devā uta muktās te kiṃ vā ke 'py eva te janāḥ

s17-v35.plain_english: The world's dignity as worship-gear is theirs — ah, something of devotees, and just lightness!
s17-v35.sanskrit_cite: pūjopakaraṇībhūtaviśvaveśena gauravam aho kim api bhaktānāṃ kim apy eva ca lāghavam

s17-v36.plain_english: From worship-made eye-throw agitation, nectar-rising for devotees — as from the gods' milk-ocean churning.

s17-v37.plain_english: Some take worship as the wish-cow; others, inward-turned, milk the nectar-stream.
s17-v37.sanskrit_cite: pūjāṃ ke cana manyante dhenuṃ kāmadughām iva sudhādhārādhikarasāṃ dhayanty antarmukhāḥ pare

s17-v38.plain_english: Even eye-throws, world-approved, bring something within — may the festival grow.
s17-v38.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānām akṣavikṣepo 'py eṣa saṃsārasaṃmataḥ upanīya kim apy antaḥ puṣṇāty arcāmahotsavam

s17-v39.plain_english: By devotion-agitation, worship in self-become-Him — wonder: poverty's top fruit is lowliness' fruit.
s17-v39.sanskrit_cite: bhaktikṣobhavaśād īśa svātmabhūte 'rcanaṃ tvayi citraṃ dainyāya no yāvad dīnatāyāḥ paraṃ phalam

s17-v40.plain_english: For some, rite is upacāra-step to His feet; for devotees, non-duality-bliss-spread.
s17-v40.sanskrit_cite: upacārapadaṃ pūjā keṣāṃ cit tvatpadāptaye bhaktānāṃ bhavadaikātmyanirvṛttiprasaras tu saḥ

s17-v41.plain_english: Spread by unbound mad devotion to the formless-seeming, it gains some foothold in You.
s17-v41.sanskrit_cite: apy asambaddharūpārcābhaktyunmādanirargalaiḥ vitanyamānā labhate pratiṣṭhāṃ tvayi kām api

s17-v42.plain_english: Taste-stunned mind; He alone as worship's vessel, they say.
s17-v42.sanskrit_cite: svādubhaktirasāsvādastabdhībhūtamanaś cyutām śambho tvam eva lalitaḥ pūjānāṃ kila bhājanam

s17-v43.plain_english: Full, pure, steady, devoted means be mine for His worship, Lord.
s17-v43.sanskrit_cite: paripūrṇāni śuddhāni bhaktimanti sthirāṇi ca bhavatpūjāvidhau nātha sādhanāni bhavantu me

s17-v44.plain_english: In the whole worship-treasure, what fortune of the organ-host blooms?
s17-v44.sanskrit_cite: aśeṣapūjāsatkośe tvatpūjākarmaṇi prabho aho karaṇavṛndasya kāpi lakṣmīr vijṛmbhate

s17-v45.plain_english: This prettiness is Yours alone, Lord: though Lord of all, worshipped by servants — and found.
s17-v45.sanskrit_cite: eṣā peśalimā nātha tavaiva kila dṛśyate viśveśvaro 'pi bhṛtyair yad arcyase yaś ca labhyase

s17-v46.plain_english: Rise from formed or formless, being or non-being — may my festival rise.
s17-v46.sanskrit_cite: sadāmurttād amūrttādvā bhāvād yad vāpy abhāvataḥ uttheyān me praśastasya bhavatpūjāmahotsavaḥ

s17-v47.plain_english: With lust, anger, pride made offering, who always worship — bow to them; of them I am pleased, in truth.
s17-v47.sanskrit_cite: kāmakrodhābhimānais tvām upaharīkṛtaiḥ sadā ye 'rcayanti namas tebhyas teṣāṃ tuṣṭo 'smi tattvataḥ

s17-v48.plain_english: Victor, Your festival of devotees' supreme rule — though made with straw, yet furnished with jewels.
s17-v48.sanskrit_cite: jayaty eṣa bhavadbhaktibhājāṃ pūjāvidhiḥ paraḥ yas tṛṇaiḥ kriyamāno 'pi ratnair evopakalpate

s18-v01.plain_english: Finding You inside the world, they get inside You — never far are Your devotees.
s18-v01.sanskrit_cite: jagato 'ntarato bhavantam āptvā punar etad bhavato 'ntarāl labhante jagadīśa tavaiva bhaktibhājo na hi teṣām iha dūrato 'sti kiñcit

s18-v02.plain_english: He here, She everywhere, pregnant with the order of all things, supreme — but at the ultimate step, no division of Her nor of the triple world.
s18-v02.sanskrit_cite: kvacid eva bhavān kvacid bhavānī sakalārthakramagarbhiṇī pradhānā paramārthapade tu naiva devyā bhavato nāpi jatattrayasya bhedaḥ

s18-v03.plain_english: The ungrateful know not the auspicious, though proud; all things, though effort-favored — but this mind, though risen, does not perceive the self-form here; ah, alas, I am destroyed.
s18-v03.sanskrit_cite: no jānate subhagam apy avalepavanto lokāḥ prayatnasubhagā nikhila hi bhāvāḥ cetaḥ punar yad idam udyatam apy avaiti naivātmarūpam iha hā tad aho hato 'smi

s18-v04.plain_english: Who has gained dwelling in the self made of You, Your feet worshipped with full wealth — needing neither food nor covering ever: to him I bow.
s18-v04.sanskrit_cite: bhavanmayasvātmanivāsalabdhasampadbharābhyarcitayuṣmadaṅghriḥ na bhojanācchādanam apy ajasram apekṣate yas tam ahaṃ nato 'smi

s18-v05.plain_english: Ever dwelling in Your body-abode yet inwardly supreme-burning, this world — by Your will make me here, of worship-joy-nature.
s18-v05.sanskrit_cite: sadā bhavaddehanivāsasvastho 'py antaḥ paraṃ dahyata eṣa lokaḥ tavecchayā tat kuru me yathātra tvadarcanānandamayo bhaveyam

s18-v06.plain_english: Spontaneously risen, touching Your lotus-feet pair, drinking the worship-nectar — mind intent, may I be, in gathering my aims, with mere touch-happiness as world-tour.

s18-v07.plain_english: In the whole field of dealings, plainly, while You throb inside, Lord — coming and going ever, may my things shine always.
s18-v07.sanskrit_cite: sakalavyavahāragocare sphuṭam antaḥ spurati tvayi prabho upayānty apayānti cāniśam mama vastūni vibhāntu sarvadā

s18-v08.plain_english: Ever in Your city, or parted and roaming — may I be, by You: never even a moment's defeat for me, where I am become of You.
s18-v08.sanskrit_cite: satatam eva tavaiva pure 'thavāpy arahito vicareyam ahaṃ tvayā kṣaṇalavo 'py atha mā sma bhavet sa me na vijaye nanu yatra bhavanmayaḥ

s18-v09.plain_english: Filled all round with cool nectar-floods streaming from Your limbs — in the wealth of worshipping You here, Your devotees move in saṃsāra's middle.
s18-v09.sanskrit_cite: bhavadaṅgaparisravatsuśītāmṛtapūrair bharite samantato 'pi bhavadarcanasampadeha bhaktās tava saṃsārasaro 'ntare caranti

s18-v10.plain_english: In the cool shade of the great-mantra tree, in Your great forest, in my own self always, Lord, may I dwell as Your worshipper.
s18-v10.sanskrit_cite: mahāmantratarucchāyāśītale tvanmahāvane nijātmani sadā nātha vaseyaṃ tava pūjakaḥ

s18-v11.plain_english: As everything living mirrors You, mirror-formed — so before me, Lord, come forth graced with three eyes and trident.
s18-v11.sanskrit_cite: prativastu samastajīvataḥ pratibhāsi pratibhāmayo yathā mama nātha tathā puraḥ prathāṃ vraja netratrayaśūlaśobhitaḥ

s18-v12.plain_english: From pride-offering, love-held devotion-built — pleased, when will You be everywhere my eyes' ground?
s18-v12.sanskrit_cite: abhimānacarūpahārato mamatābhaktibhareṇa kalpitāt paritoṣagataḥ kadā bhavān mama sarvatra bhaved dṛśaḥ padam

s18-v13.plain_english: Dwelling in the nectar-ocean middle, mind drowned in Your worship-rite alone — may I do all people's business, tasting everything everywhere.
s18-v13.sanskrit_cite: nivasanparamāmṛtābdhimadhye bhavadarcāvidhimātramagnacittaḥ sakalaṃ janavṛttam ācareyaṃ rasayan sarvata eva kiñcanāpi

s18-v14.plain_english: Your thing here, Your truth — who is fit to disclose the matter? This same name-form-sport-unequalled of Yours takes away — since You are Hara, the Taker.
s18-v14.sanskrit_cite: bhavadīyam ihāstu vastu tattvaṃ vivarītuṃ ka ivātra pātram arthe idam eva hi nāmarūpaceṣṭādyasamaṃ te harate haro 'si yasmāt

s18-v15.plain_english: For peace, no hankering for pleasure at all, among those drunk with devotion amassed — nor even begging the fruit of seeking liberation remembered before the heart-thief.
s18-v15.sanskrit_cite: śāntaye na sukhalipsutā manāg bhaktisambhṛtamadeṣu taiḥ prabhoḥ mokṣamārgaṇaphalāpi nārthanā smaryate hṛdayahāriṇaḥ puraḥ

s18-v16.plain_english: Waking or other state, or any beyond, while slightly steady — for the devotee-people, all is Your festival in the ever-present mind.
s18-v16.sanskrit_cite: jāgaretaradaśāthavā parā yāpi kācana manāg avasthiteḥ bhaktibhājanajanasya sākhilā tvatsanāthamanaso mahotsavaḥ

s18-v17.plain_english: Mind's eye-wheel courses, everywhere loosened yet still — reaching You, of firm-long awareness: Lord, how, by devotion-wealth's heat?
s18-v17.sanskrit_cite: āmano 'kṣavalayasya vṛttayaḥ sarvataḥ śithilavṛttayo 'pi tāḥ tvām avāpya dṛḍhadīrghasaṃvido nātha bhaktidhanasoṣmaṇāṃ katham

s18-v18.plain_english: Nothing divided was left uncreated, no non-pleasure unmade here — yet all suffers and divides in every way: bow to the wonder-abode.
s18-v18.sanskrit_cite: na ca vibhinnam asṛjyata kiñcid asty atha sukhetarad atra na nirmitam atha ca duḥkhi ca bhedi ca sarvathāpy asamavismayadhāma namo 'stu te

s18-v19.plain_english: Of me whose thought-stain is washed bright by hard-denier nectar-filling flood, whose unconquered-doubt-foe is crushed — may Your sight be unbroken.

s18-v20.plain_english: Enter me plainly, then may I enter Thee — always, Lord, for I am Thine: with violent speed may I worship Thy body face to face.
s18-v20.sanskrit_cite: sphuṭam aviśa mām athāviśeyaṃ satataṃ nātha bhavantamasmi yasmāt rabhasena vapus tavaiva sākṣāt paramāsattigataḥ samarcayeyam

s18-v21.plain_english: In You no one's is praise-power — yet it exists since You are so beautiful; my constant prayer again is this: that I behold You, Lord, unwearied.
s18-v21.sanskrit_cite: tvayi na stutiśaktir asti kasyāpy athavāsty eva yato 'tisundaro 'si satataṃ punar arthitaṃ mamaitad yad aviśrānti vilokayeyam īśam

s19-v01.plain_english: Beyond prayer-grounds, strange-fruit-giver — victorious, unprecedented in story, Śiva the true wish-tree.

s19-v02.plain_english: Since from the One container all is got through the self, from You — yet this own self of mine does not join Thee, the Highest — her.
s19-v02.sanskrit_cite: sarvavastuni ca yaikanidhānāt svātmanas tvad akhilaṃ kila labhyam asya me punar asau nijā ātmā na tvam eva ghaṭase paramās tām

s19-v03.plain_english: The self, knowledge-action-formed consciousness-body, is in every way the Lord alone — but would there even be a body among all these things, or what else?
s19-v03.sanskrit_cite: jñānakarmamayacidvapur ātmā sarvathaiṣa parameśvara eva syād vapus tu nikhileṣu padārtheṣv eṣu nāma na bhavet kim utānyat

s19-v04.plain_english: By unequalled fruit, stealing pain — melt into His sight-natured form; may my going be His-formed.
s19-v04.sanskrit_cite: viṣamārtimuṣānena phalena tvaddṛgātmanā abhilīya pathā nātha mamāstu tvanmayī gatiḥ

s19-v05.plain_english: When will foot-thought-jewel-creeper-fruition, amazing the perfected, befall me, from You?
s19-v05.sanskrit_cite: bhavadamalacaraṇacintāratnalatālaṅkṛtā kadā siddhiḥ siddhajanamānasānāṃ vismayajananī ghaṭeta mama bhavataḥ

s19-v06.plain_english: When, Lord, shall I fully see Your pure face-orb, from which streams unprecedented nectar-flood, which drowns the whole world?
s19-v06.sanskrit_cite: karhi nātha vimalaṃ mukhabimbaṃ tāvakaṃ samavalokayitāsmi yatsravaty amṛtapūram apūrvaṃ yo nimajjayati viśvam aśeṣam

s19-v07.plain_english: Your form, risen at mere meditation — when, Lord, will it ever fill with supreme-nectar floods my far gaps named non-duality-liberation?
s19-v07.sanskrit_cite: dhyātamātramuditaṃ tava rūpaṃ karhi nātha paramāmṛtapūraiḥ pūrayet tvadavibhedavimokṣākhyātidūravivarāṇi sadā me

s19-v08.plain_english: By touch of Your peerless rasa, unroaming abandoned — not even now is my mind, Lord: when will it be? Let it be soon.
s19-v08.sanskrit_cite: tvadīyānuttararasāsaṅgasaṃtyaktacāpalam nādyāpi me mano nātha karhi syād astu śīghrataḥ

s19-v09.plain_english: Not dry-bitter things only — bring on all, always, gained by offering to You; let even opposites befall me.
s19-v09.sanskrit_cite: mā śuṣkakaṭukāny eva paraṃ sarvāṇi sarvadā tavopahṛtya labdhāni dvandvāny apy āpatantu me

s19-v10.plain_english: Lord, may Your pure rays come face to face, as long as body-mind-heat-dark is wiped out.
s19-v10.sanskrit_cite: nātha sāṃmukhyam āyāntu viśuddhās tava raśmayaḥ yāvat kāyamanastāpatamobhiḥ parilupyatām

s19-v11.plain_english: God, be gracious till my path-blockers, truth-stealing, sense-thieves are tamed.
s19-v11.sanskrit_cite: deva prasīda yāvan me tvanmārgaparipanthikāḥ paramārthamuṣo vaśyā bhūyāsur guṇataskarāḥ

s19-v12.plain_english: With Your devotion-nectar-essence fill my mind fast, Lord — till these are carried off, drowned: all sapless habits.
s19-v12.sanskrit_cite: tvad bhaktisudhāsārair mānasam āpūryatāṃ mamāśu vibho yāvad imā uhyantāṃ niḥśeṣāsāravāsanāḥ plutvā

s19-v13.plain_english: In liberation-state, where is devotion to You — how could it shine even for the mortal-natured? So set me, Unborn, on a fitting attainment-ground.
s19-v13.sanskrit_cite: mokṣadaśāyāṃ bhaktis tvayi kuta iva martyadharmiṇo 'pi na sā rājati tato 'nurūpām āropaya siddhibhūmikām aja mām

s19-v14.plain_english: Greedy for a siddhi-drop's gain, don't settle proud me — thin is liberation beside Your devotion-face's sprouting aṇimā-wings.
s19-v14.sanskrit_cite: siddhilavalābhalubdhaṃ mām avalepena mā vibho saṃsthāḥ kṣāmas tvadbhaktimukhe prollasadaṇimādipakṣato mokṣaḥ

s19-v15.plain_english: May the Lord be pleased with me, His slave — I ask only this, since the three-worlds Giver exceeds my sight.
s19-v15.sanskrit_cite: dāsasya me prasīdatu bhagavān etāvad eva nanu yāce dātā tribhuvananātho yasya na tanmādṛśāṃ dṛśo viṣayaḥ

s19-v16.plain_english: In mind full of Your body-mindfulness-nectar-rasa, may Your lotus-feet-pair bloom in mine, ever dripping honey, supramundane.
s19-v16.sanskrit_cite: tvadvapuḥsmṛtisudhārasapūrṇe mānase tava padāmbujayugmam māmake vikasad astu sadaiva prasravanmadhu kim apy atilokam

s19-v17.plain_english: I have a Lord, a father — Tryambaka — and a mother, Bhavānī; no second exists for me here — thus most-fulfilled may I roam.
s19-v17.sanskrit_cite: asti me prabhur asau janako 'tha tryambako 'tha jananī ca bhavānī na dvitīya iha ko 'pi mamāstīty eva nirvṛtatamo vicareyam

s20-v01.plain_english: Bow to the three-worlds' Lord, ash-white, three-eyed, trident-bearing, snake-threaded, moon-crested.
s20-v01.sanskrit_cite: nathaṃ tribhuvananāthaṃ bhūtisitaṃ trinayanaṃ triśūladharam upavītīkṛtabhoginam indukalāśekharaṃ vande

s20-v02.plain_english: I praise, self-forgetting, white-robed in bite-torn cloth, dancing to the tune of the skull-garland.

s20-v03.plain_english: Bow to those whose god is Hara, whose acts are Hara-fit, whose lives lean wholly to Hara — the fortunate abodes.
s20-v03.sanskrit_cite: vande tān daivataṃ yeṣāṃ haraś ceṣṭā harocitāḥ haraikapravaṇāḥ prāṇāḥ sadā saubhāgyasadmanām

s20-v04.plain_english: Your play, behind lordship — and this too, as wished-fulfilled in gifts, by self I reach the supreme means.
s20-v04.sanskrit_cite: krīḍitaṃ tava maheśvaratāyāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nyad idam eva yathaitat iṣṭamātraghaṭiteṣv avadāneṣv ātmanā param upāyam upaimi

s20-v05.plain_english: In Your world-venerated abode, in this play — how great would my bliss-birth be?
s20-v05.sanskrit_cite: tvaddhāmni viśvavandye 'sminn iyati krīḍane sati tava nātha kiyān bhūyānn ānandarasasambhavaḥ

s20-v06.plain_english: How could He not be fortunate — Hara, Gauri's beloved? And how could Hara not be Gauri's supreme beloved?
s20-v06.sanskrit_cite: kathaṃ sa subhago mā bhūdyo gauryā vallabho haraḥ haro 'pi mā bhūd atha kiṃ gauryāḥ paramavallabhaḥ

s20-v07.plain_english: Whose meditation-nectar is undying, self-rooted, ever-fresh consciousness-creepers, like some tree of being.
s20-v07.sanskrit_cite: dhyānāmṛtamayaṃ yasya svātmamūlam anaśvaram saṃvillatās tathārūpās tasya kasyāpi sattaroḥ

s20-v08.plain_english: At devotion-itch's showing, Lord's pillar-firmness arises — by it the world, great festival, is won.
s20-v08.sanskrit_cite: bhaktikaṇḍūsam ullāsāvasare parameśvara mahānikaṣapāṣāṇasthūṇā pūjaiva jāyate

s20-v09.plain_english: Ever to creation-sport, ever seated in staying-pleasure, ever world-eating-sated — to the Master, bow.
s20-v09.sanskrit_cite: sadā srṣṭivinodāya sadā sthitisukhāsine sadā tribhuvanāhāratṛptāya svāmine namaḥ

s20-v10.plain_english: Nowhere gone, nothing left — who see Your abode as to-be here, fortunate: bow to them.
s20-v10.sanskrit_cite: na kvāpi gatvā hitvāpi na kiṃcid idam eva ye bhavyaṃ tvaddhāma paśyanti bhavyās tebhyo namo namaḥ

s20-v11.plain_english: For the devotion-fortuned, what else is begged; for the devotion-poor, what else is begged?
s20-v11.sanskrit_cite: bhaktilakṣmīsamṛddhānāṃ kim anyad upayācitam etayā vā daridraṇāṃ kim anyad upayācitam

s20-v12.plain_english: Where pains turn pleasures, poison turns nectar, saṃsāra turns liberation — that path is Śiva.
s20-v12.sanskrit_cite: duḥkhāny api sukhāyante viṣam apy amṛtāyate mokṣāyate ca saṃsāro yatra mārgaḥ sa śaṅkaraḥ

s20-v13.plain_english: At root, middle, end, no suffering for Your people — yet we sink, Lord: tell why.
s20-v13.sanskrit_cite: mūle madhye 'vasāne ca nāsti duḥkhaṃ bhavajjuṣāṃ tathāpi vayam īśāna sīdāmaḥ katham ucyatām

s20-v14.plain_english: Light is worth begging even by others, beginners in knowledge-yoga — You, Lord of devotees, are like the light of the free.
s20-v14.sanskrit_cite: jñānayogādinānyeṣām apy apekṣitum arhati prakāśaḥ svairiṇām iva bhavān bhaktimatāṃ prabho

s20-v15.plain_english: Devotees have no prayers, no remembrance of You the self — yet this "Śiva" of theirs, something, on the lip.
s20-v15.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānāṃ nārtayo nāpy asty ādhyānaṃ svātmanas tava tathāpy asti śivety etat kim apy eṣāṃ bahirmukhe

s20-v16.plain_english: Who lights all appearances, wrapped in vimarśa — "I am this": I praise Your action-power, Lord.
s20-v16.sanskrit_cite: sarvābhāsāvabhāso yo vimarśavalito 'khilam aham etad iti staumi tāṃ kriyāśaktim īśa te

s20-v17.plain_english: All beings, from Brahmā to Viṣṇu, being devoured — so I bow, God, to the world as Your-formed.
s20-v17.sanskrit_cite: vartante jantavo 'śeṣā api brahmendraviṣṇavaḥ grasamānās tato vande deva viśvaṃ bhavanmayam

s20-v18.plain_english: All beyond Me is false, by relation to destruction — thus engaged, Lord, by Your destruction-play alone.
s20-v18.sanskrit_cite: sato vināśasambandhān matparaṃ nikhilaṃ mṛṣā evamevodyate nātha tvayā saṃhāralīlayā

s20-v19.plain_english: Meditated, Your form stands present for devotion-rich — unconquered by unthinkable-wonder-makers.
s20-v19.sanskrit_cite: dhyātam ātmupatiṣṭhata eva tvadvapur varada bhaktidhanānām apy acintyam akhilādbhutacintākartṛtāṃ prati ca te vijayante

s20-v20.plain_english: By Your devotion-wine-taste nerves' thrill, night-heroes dance, roused by vetālas.
s20-v20.sanskrit_cite: tāvakabhaktirasāsavasekād iva sukhitamarmamaṇḍalasphuritaiḥ nṛtyati vīrajano niśi vetālakulaiḥ kṛtotsāhaḥ

s20-v21.plain_english: The praise begun with this limb of mine — by it may all this time be firmly unending.
s20-v21.sanskrit_cite: ārabdhā bhavadabhinutir amunā yenāṅgakena mama śambho tenāparyantam imaṃ kālaṃ dṛḍham akhilam eva bhaviṣīṣṭa

essence: Devotion stands rule-free and self-young: undawned by method, unaged by road-dust, at home in the Lord's city, thriving on every ground (vv1-6).
Its ground proved: all beings love the self, the self is consciousness — so love stands on its own nature; knowing this by drowning is conquest (v7).

Consequences drawn: the world turns ritual ground, joy/sorrow/bewilderment all become the road, special-state localization is the one cheat — closing with the pain-seed mind ripened to freedom's fruit (vv8-26).

sections.SUMMARY: It establishes devotion without preparatory rule as valid, then proves it: since all beings desire the self and the self alone is consciousness, love directed at it stands on its own nature and needs no external ground. Knowing this by immersion is itself the conquest. The remaining verses draw the consequences — the world becomes ritual ground, every road works, localization of the goal in special states is the one deceit — and close by transfiguring the opening image: the dust-greyed mind, watered by devotion, fruits liberation.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of establishment (pratiṣṭhā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at devotion without preparatory rule. The rasa is the tranquility of methodless devotion — not a means among means but the thing itself. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as bhakti-rasa: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the sole beloved. Kṣemarāja's commentary: devotion without preparatory rule is valid because all beings desire the self and the self alone is consciousness.

essence: Twenty-nine salutations perform the all-self: every stuff of the world — fire, moon, gods, still, moving — named as His, every verse landing bowed (whole song).

Each bow names Him by paradox pairs — cool fire and devourer, Veda-foe and Veda-maker, round's cause and foe, ever-bound and ever-free, all rites and rite-free — the namaḥ holding both poles (vv1-22).
The litany turns to close: from Him to His dread power-ring (v23), from knowing to embracing (v24), from victory-cries to shelter-surrender (vv25-29).

sections.SUMMARY: It performs contemplation of the all-self as twenty-nine salutations. Each verse names Śiva by a paradoxical pair — cool fire and devourer, Veda-breaker and Veda-maker, saṃsāra's cause and foe, ever-bound and ever-free, all rites and no rite — and the *namaḥ* addressed to both poles at once is itself the recognition that opposites coincide only in Him. The litany closes by turning from Him to His terrible powers (23), from knowing to embracing (24), and from victory-cries to refuge (29).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as contemplation of the all-self
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of contemplation (paribhāvanā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at opposites coinciding only in Him. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual contemplation — twenty-nine salutations naming Śiva by paradoxical pairs, each namaḥ a recognition that opposites coincide only in Him. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the all-self.

essence: The third beyond being and non-being: leap the two-yoked course; freedom contagious among the unfree — Thy hangers-on live free (vv01-02, v18).
Love's instruments: remembrance-medicine, begged moon-glance, heart-union vessel, flooding meditation, Śiva-din that routs pain — arrival roared and danced (vv03-11, v13).
Supremacy without second: moon-crowned high Lord, cancelled yogas, play-lake ocean, shamed miseries, beads told inside oneness, knower in known — closing keen and swoon (vv04, v12, vv14-17, vv19-21).

sections.SUMMARY: It is affection's logic: leap over being and non-being to the third (1); find freedom contagious among the unfree (2); take remembrance as medicine (3); crown Him moon-umbrella king (4); beg one glance (5); interrogate one's own dryness (6); mark unmelted hearts contemptible (7); make heart-union the vessel of powers (8); let meditation flood joys and sorrows alike (9); never part, more than self (10); roar and dance arrival (11); cancel other knowables and yogas (12); let Śiva-sound chase sorrows (13); deny any second great person (14); shrink the ocean to a play-lake by servitude (15); shame miseries by manifestation (16); recite inside supremacy (17); tie the knot of being-non-being (18); face the unseen all-pervading brightness (19); find the knower inside the known (20); and close crying sharp in knowing bewilderment (21).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of affection (praṇaya); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the third beyond being/non-being. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śṛṅgāra: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as beloved.

essence: Confession and approach: fickle mind praised for refuge-worship, low ground kept past gods' stairs, one road begged with world-doings shuttered (vv1-3).
Praise and petition: name-cries, foot-lotus throne and sap, light-body nearness, nectar-smeared mind, will-set walking, heart-blooms, fattened love, fresh hundredfold Name (vv4-13).

Longing's triumph and paradox: Śiva-din winners, bolted city unknocked, face-lotus hunger, serfdom fitness, unheard wail, omens, Śiva-night, sapless overlordship, tough self-bond, worshiper-shaped God (vv14-25).

sections.SUMMARY: It is direct address under unfitness: the fickle mind praised for turning (1), the lowest ground kept after arrival (2), reveal-and-hide demanded with use-me-now (3), a spell of names (4); then the world re-seen — Brahmā laughed at (5), nothing apart from His body (6), two tastes of one dust (7), flash-devotion (8), discernment demanding plain manifestation (9), placed-unasked complaint (10); then love's evidence — blooming gods (11), separation-talk fruiting (12), the sideways-entering word (13), winning faces (14); then the impasse and its passage — finished world, unknocked door (15), just-a-little asked (16), knowing self-accusation (17), tasting-frequency fitness (18), others blind but MY cry heard (19); then exchange and arrival — pleasures recalled to be exchanged (20), hundreds of omens (21), the shining night (22), empire tasteless (23), the knot He tied (24), and the final inversion: the worshipped stays the worshipper, shining in seers' bodies (25).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of demand (prārthanā) and confession (āvedana); the vyabhicāri is compassion (karuṇa) at the devotee's unfitness. The rasa is the devotion of the unfit — demanding, complaining, crying out — proving that unfitness is no bar to address. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as bhakti: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute addressed by one who is unworthy yet addresses anyway. The stotra negotiates: demand (dehi, kuru, prakaṭaya), complaint (placed-unasked), and crying out (MY cry heard).

essence: Approaching touches: foot-brush joined, dust-dyed hair, dumb dwelling, shouted dance, half-shut gaping, mountain-mind, Her town, opening heart-lotus (vv1-8).
Tasting deepens: wax mind, bursting pot, oozing cool, lake-diving, offered passions, sated glance, straw worship, unparted feasting, secondless fullness (vv9-17).
Vows and vastness: foot-place won, perfume hardened, clash taught, frenzy willed, vanguard run, unre-said sap, vast roamed, dust-kept thought, sole-touchers shown (vv18-26).

sections.SUMMARY: It is a practice-manual in 26 assignments: bring-me-by-the-neck (1), when-shall-I-dance (2), silence over wisdom (3), exclamation as liturgy (4), half-closed eyes (5), dwelling defined by practice (6), the divine household (7), heart-lotus blooming (8), wax-melting (9), appear regardless (10), streaming both ways (11), pleasure beyond pleasures (12), cooking passions into shared nectar (13), one glance at servants (14), self-address as Śiva (15), gaining without leaving (16), desire's end (17), the festival as destination (18), perfume against stink (19), instruct the contradicting heart (20), passing through yogic states (21), devotion as vanguard (22), the Name's infinity with unrepeatable taste (23), roaming not arriving (24), self-sufficiency except foot-dust (25), the flash where the world melts (26).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of vanguard (puraḥsara); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) of the devotee's own strength. The rasa is the heroism of devotion going before every faculty — speech, mind, body — so the devotee never faces anything unaccompanied. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as vīra: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the sole vanguard. The stotra is a practice-manual in 26 assignments: bring-me-by-the-neck, when-shall-I-dance, silence over wisdom, exclamation as liturgy, half-closed eyes, dwelling defined by practice, divine household, heart-lotus blooming, wax-melting, appear regardless, streaming both ways, pleasure beyond pleasures, cooking passions into shared nectar, one glance at servants, self-address as Śiva, gaining without leaving, desire's end, festival as destination, perfume against stink, instruct the contradicting heart, passing through yogic states, devotion as vanguard, Name's infinity, roaming not arriving, self-sufficiency except foot-dust, flash where world melts.

essence: Separation held in nearness: parted instants, pithed passing, held longing, and the final hunt — love kept unparted through parting (vv1-2, v5, v11).
Truth shown and won: body-speech-mind oneness, matched praise, melting clouds, jewel-light, ground everywhere, limb-embrace joy (vv3-4, vv6-10).

sections.SUMMARY: Separation itself becomes the method: burning to be seen (1), unparted-in-Him while parted-from-world (2), all goings as Him (3), speech matching His bliss (4), roaming desireless in His possession (5), contentment ending toil (6), things melting skyward (7), the jewel blazing from His middle (8), arrival everywhere by effortlessness (9), embrace by mere will (10) — then the single imperative: appear, with all other prayers renounced (11).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as the path bursting forth
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of burning (tāpa) and seeing (paśyan); the vyabhicāri is effortlessness (anāyāsa) and contentment (santuṣṭi). The rasa is the tranquility of the path bursting forth — burning to be seen, then effortlessness.

essence: Melting and entry: same-sap minds dropping disaster, axes of certainty on passion's root, melting stain-strings (vv1-3).
Mother and ripening: wallowing fed sap on sap to sky-going, connoisseurship won, mind-jewel spark-shed (vv4-6).
Station won: full-throated hymning past waiting gods, whole-sensed seeing, wed mind-lad hardening mine-thought (vv7-9).

sections.SUMMARY: The mind is cured by drowning: dropped in the bliss-ocean (1), axed at the mine/not-mine root (2), melted then blazing (3), mother-fed till winged (4), skilled in tasting (5), sun-melted of wax-drops (6), praising where gods wait outside (7), seeing world-as-Śiva through frenzy (8), and finally remarried — the mind-boy wedding the devotion-maiden and hardening a new mine (9).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of victory (vijaya) over distress (vidhura); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) of the mind's cure. The rasa is the tranquility of victory — domestic allegory making the mind's cure narratable.

essence: Grace nears: grace-drop and nearing devotion rooting each in other, chewed mastery raising contentment, worldlike thirst (vv1-3).
Senses gathered: body-grounds, thrill-seats, possession-pictured striding (vv4-6).
Blooming and union: Thou-natured bloom, dread gorge filled, dusted turning, lotus-lake wading, supreme shimmer, joy-mad limbs, plain-shining resolve (vv7-13).

sections.SUMMARY: Grace-drop above and devotion rising below: it watches their meeting produce unworldly upsurge — chewing lordship (2), thirsting with unconstructed sight (3), demanding plainness in both registers (4), seating the faculties (5), exceeding all dealings in a possession-body (6), blooming and joining into untellability (7), flooding the dread gorge (8); then the wager — union-drops against world-pleasures, with double-fall risk named (9); hamsa-and-stalk botany joining below, inside, above (10); all things under thought's scope without seizure (11); practice for catastrophe — limb joined, joy-mad (12); and the closing epistemology: woven in Him, shown by Him, certain — shine (13).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of upsurge (udbala); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the grace-devotion meeting and vertigo of the possession-body. The rasa is the tranquility of unworldly upsurge — not worldly excitement but the peace of exceeding all dealings. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute's unworldly upsurge.

essence: Twenty when-questions that are really one: when will longing become meeting — asked of mind, face, gods, world, yoga, pride, tears, beast-life, play, speech (vv1-19).
Answered once, in the last verse: by hugging hard and seeing without effort — strainless full beholding (v20).

sections.SUMMARY: Twenty when-questions that are really one: when will longing become meeting? It asks it of the mind (1), the face (2), needlessness (3), the gods (4), distinction (5), the slow (6), flight (7), the world (8), knowledge and yoga (9), all hearers (10), transparency (11), leadership (12), pride (13), lying down (14), the far shore (15), tears (16), beast-life (17), play (18), speech (19) — and answers it once, in the last verse: by hugging hard and seeing without effort (20).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as the victory of autonomy
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of longing (utsuka); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the twentyfold kadā that never leaves Him. The rasa is the tranquility of autonomy — freedom desiring only itself; the victory is that the questions never leave Him. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the sole object of longing.

essence: Complaint and nearness: Great-One's men levelled, trailers tasting, husband ending death, wink-won All (vv1-4).

Vision's catalogue: moon-drop, sun-spark, third-eye badge, seen joys, city in-making, uneven eyes, might-less being, stayed mind, roaming selves, company-ripened, slave-borne, hunger past-past, ghee-joined pains (vv5-16).
Paradox and seal: fit unreality-show, breathed strands, I-less world, dissolving great, dark range, nectar-nature, speech-jewel, effortless ripening, slave's drink, devouring fire (vv17-26).

sections.SUMMARY: It breaks non-separation by showing it was never sameness: devotees and worldlings share one world but eat differently (1–4); cosmic lights shrink to droplets (5–6); seeing runs both directions at once (7); the pleased drag the world inside (8); all looks same-eyed but for the Uneven-eyed Seer (9); deniers depend on Him (10); the whole path conditional on standing (11); same wandering, different placement (12); mere conduct perfects (13); servants claim bearing (14); vision leaves touch hungry (15); ghee makes sorrows bearable (16); unreality permitted by omnipotence (17); qualities dance, breathed by Him (18); ego the prop of manifestation (19); anger-fire purifies (20); daylight accuses (21); all nectar, yet sole mortality-house (22); name-and-bow-mark empower (23); ease-by-identity demanded (24); slave-and-self, gods sated through him (25); eater-fire between heart and navel closes (26).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of discrimination (viveka); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the pairs that refuse to merge. The rasa is the tranquility of non-dual recognition that survives difference — not the thrill of sorting but the peace of seeing all as one while holding difference. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute breaking continuity without breaking oneness.

essence: Begging ground: world unowned, outright begging, straw-lordship, unwoven praise, dream-question (vv1-5).
Self-confessed lowliness: scent-speck, heart-word split, dull litany, ear-pearls, death-wounded power-seeking (vv6-10).
High praise and rescue: vocative catalogue, makerhood questioned, life-drink hankered, smasher begged, gloom-smasher bowed (vv11-15).

sections.SUMMARY: Dispossession (nothing mine, 1) → begging that begs (2) → straw thrones, sterile merit (3) → unblocked praise (4) → even in dream (5) → fragrance-dot transfiguring (6) → one work only (7) → resume of disqualifications (8) → trifles to pearls (9) → even cheating devotion works (10) → litany as battering-ram (11) → cornered metaphysics, clinging while harassed (12) → approved suffering, chosen longevity (13) → skilled destroyer, act now (14) → bow to the sole work and over-bright light (15).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of longing (utsuka); the vyabhicāri is trust (viśvasita) that keeps begging from despair. The rasa is the tranquility of longing-trust — dispossession plus longing plus trust as a complete path. The title names it: Autsukyaviśvasita (Yearning and assurance). Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as sole object of longing, with trust as the stabilizing vyabhicāri.

essence: Seeing opened: no helper, no bar — flooded all, self-arising beheld, creation trickled, nectar tasted, timeless seeing, yoga ripened, sported words, feet-dwelt (vv1-8).
Dwelling deepened: foot-lotus belly, sham resolve, drunk Lord, pith-gist taken, indwelling births, soundless churn, Goddess seat, slipping mark, nectar current, grain of groundedness (vv9-18).

Beholding sealed: measured beholding, limb-going, plough-gait seeing, unstopped feast, sayings, limb-dawn, strayed ranges, born slavery, counter-stance keenness, things-as-things, naught-asserted won (vv19-29).

sections.SUMMARY: Twenty-nine approximations that cancel themselves: no helper, no hinderer (1); sourced yet self-born (2); how could things reach His path (3); the sated wander (4); timeless vision (5); entering by resolve (6); pure play (7); fearless dwelling (8); dissolved, drunk, wandering (9); pretense suffices (10); one-taste drinking (11); the essence-extract (12); inside/outside puzzle (13); facing everywhere in agitation (14); reveal the abode (15); fled yet never unseen (16); flood to joy (17); grain for worship-exchange (18); seeing each thing, seeing You (19); unhaunting mind questioned (20); ploughmen see (21); feast unstopped (22); insight, power, unpausing worship (23); sense-heap as His limb (24); roaming mind, skilled service (25); slave by His will, yet faceless (26); opponents wondered at (27); things as things by His being (28); nothing/something grammar of worship (29).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as pointing to the secret
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of pointing (nirdeśa); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at approximations that cancel themselves. The rasa is the tranquility of pointing — no exposition, only indication; each verse a finger, none the moon. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute pointed to, never stated.

essence: Mark and frame: pain-joy mark heard, unshowing black wiped, live-die-or-else in His frame (vv1-3).

Work's fabric: lovers' pride shining, birth from nectar-telling, thought-seen-touched chain, grounded pair, sense-wine madness, known unknowns, quartered service, unweighed power-fall, shining beholding, palace rest, offered relish (vv4-13).
Widening close: all-widening flashing, whirling thing-ring, poison-nectar, prattle ditties, unwilled will, bottomless devouring entered and praised (vv14-20).

sections.SUMMARY: It defines pain as separation and pleasure as union (v.1), then proves the definition across twenty moves: the impure instant wiped (2), abiding unto death (3), pride sanctified (4), perception-as-it-stands as fitness (5), meditation-vision-touch sequence (6), the mutually grounding pair of seeing and festival (7), drinking through every sense (8), the country with no other (9), slavery as fitness (10), grace that never deliberates turned back on its delay (11), beholding with one's own hands inside and out (12), ascent by mere wish (13), worship answering touch (14), joy swelling the world (15), fearlessness as perception's corollary (16), poison turned nectar by stance (17), songs wanted otherwise (18), the uncountable play that withholds the cup (19), entering-and-praising the fathomless (20).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of rehearsal (abhyāsa); the vyabhicāri is clarity (prasāda) of the whole path compressed into recitable moves. The rasa is the tranquility of daily rehearsal — definition, purification, pride, perception, worship, grace-logic, ascent, cosmology, refuge in one sitting. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute summarized. Lakshmanjoo's commentary on v.13 compares grace to Scotch Whisky — the rasa is intoxication-without-intoxication, the bliss of abiding in the Lord's abode.

essence: Faces hailed: taste, Rudra-One, brow-eye, powers-body, other-world dress, milk-sea shade, cool-digit shelter, hallowing touch (vv1-8).
Deeds hailed: duping sillies, love-gifts, Brahmā-might, sealed glory, creation-wish, striding worlds, inborn height, burn-work, nectar-sea, delusion-lamp (vv9-18).
Nearness and finale: life's-life warbling, gold-vein mountain, pain-unneared, leafed dependents, bright deed, victory-vessel and thirteenfold hail to Three-eyed (vv19-24).

sections.SUMMARY: It is a victory-litany: twenty-four *jaya*-cries that praise the Lord by letting every attribute stand absolute — names (2–3), body and feet (4), beauty and adornment (5–8), duping and embrace (9), greed for gifts (10), outlasting the gods (11), sealing worlds and giving the self (12), secondlessness with a helper (13), stride and song (14), need-free height (15), unopposed terror (16), play and anger (17), lamp and wakefulness (18), cave-hum and mind-sky (19), gold-mountain and portent-moon (20), missed-by-austerity and seen-by-madness (21), leafing and fondling (22), sole doing and lotus-festival (23) — until the cries themselves run to thirteen and end in the three-eyed One (24).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of acclamation (jaya); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the Lord's attributes. The rasa is the heroism of praise — each cry performs conquest over silence. Twenty-four jaya-cries that praise the Lord by letting every attribute stand absolute: names, body, feet, beauty, adornment, duping, embrace, greed for gifts, outlasting gods, sealing worlds, giving self, secondlessness with helper, stride, song, need-free height, unopposed terror, play, anger, lamp, wakefulness, cave-hum, mind-sky, gold-mountain, portent-moon, missed-by-austerity, seen-by-madness, leafing, fondling, sole doing, lotus-festival — until the cries run to thirteen and end in the three-eyed One. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as vīra: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute celebrated, not argued. Lakshmanjoo's commentary: the victory-litany converts understanding into praise.

essence: Lovers against the qualified: books and far-siders set beside lover-truth; Māyā-food strollers, babblers past praise-words, masterless, dragging, selved, blind-shining, gleaner-ruling, wallowing climbers (vv1-9).
Kept and questioned: guarded hoard, dropped envy, milk-jar won, past-compare attainment, sunk gem-creeper, wonderless worry (vv10-15).
Pervasion and road: cross-scented scents, Śiva-night worship, goodness widened, far-far road walked moon-crowned (vv16-19).

sections.SUMMARY: It defines the devotee against every spiritual résumé — not the book-washed, not the yogin, not the scholar, not the detached, not the master, not the liberation-seeker — but the drunk (1–4); then shows devotion working: drawing the outer inside (5), tasting the unnamed something between all pairs (6), outshining disfigurement (7) and rank (8), rolling yet climbing on mind-worship (9); guards it as the only wealth (10), prays away jealousy toward the Goddess (11), churns the milk-ocean past curd-greed (12), declares growth itself the attainment (13) — then confesses the buried gem (14) and the worry over missing powers (15), notes praise perfuming even the hostile (16) and worship continuing in total darkness (17), prays expansion-through-dissolution (18), and closes with wasted life offered for long fortune (19).

rasa.sthayibhava: bhakti (devotion) as the devotee's defining mood
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of definition (lakṣaṇa); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) of the devotee against every spiritual résumé. The rasa is the tranquility of devotion — not a means among means but the thing itself. Bhakti is not a means among means; it is the thing yogins/scholars/ascetics circle without entering. The devotee is defined against every spiritual résumé — not the book-washed, not the yogin, not the scholar, not the detached, not the master, not the liberation-seeker — but the drunk. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as bhakti-rasa: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the sole beloved. Lakshmanjoo's commentary: bhakti is the highest path to advaita, and the devotee is equal to Śiva and even higher than Indra, Viṣṇu, Brahmā.

essence: Veil and youth: unveiled veiling, laddered method, laughed winning, undrying sap, unmet befalling, no-other-prayer (vv1-6).

Frenzy catalogue: raging Śiva-yells, pit-weeping-laughing-scatter, unfelt feeling, thrill-needles, ripened feasting, held ranges, wiped duality, straying splits, stainless minds, conquered gloom, bath-drink rites, praised world-faring (vv7-18).

Freedom and seal: ripe-love freedom named, pain-welcomed, mutual gladdening, nectar-shaped selves, shown worlds, hidden-high love cried, beauty-ground, knower-road wins, hall-clasping, dissolution feast, commanded-free lordship (vv19-30).

sections.SUMMARY: No block for folk or devotees (1); the self seen at once despite ladders (2); laughing victors and vanquished (3); no dryness, no release-seeking (4); as unknown before, may it grow (5); the single prayer (6); drunk, angry, leaping, shouting Śiva (7); crisis or peace, tears or laughter — by devotion (8); nothing to be known, inside or out (9); rejoicing even at abusers (10); pain ripening to enjoyment (11); held everywhere, same touch-joy (12); duality's double-refuge dissolved (13); pilgrim-eyes err, Being shines (14); ripened mind unmannered (15); knowledge-rich put to shame (16); devotion-nectar-drink-and-bath as rite (17); world-life praiseworthy (18); liberation renamed as ripe devotion (19); pain invited, pleasure refused (20); mutual dependence blessed, not solved (21); form or formless, always nectar (22); another world-stand in this world (23); devotion, devotion, something (24); I weep, let fierce devotion be mine (25); jewel or straw, stuck to You priceless (26); unparted, they win (27); embraced in saṃsāra's hall (28); hugging Śiva with the feasting Goddess (29); sovereignty with no subjects, otherness by which the world shines as it does not (30).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of bursting (udbheda); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) that nothing stands between devotee and Him. The rasa is the heroism of bursting bonds — no people, no gods, no method-ladders, no impurity, no sorrow, no logic stands between. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as vīra: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute unblocked. Lakshmanjoo: pāśānudbheda — bursting of the noose from inside, not cut from outside. Mutual dependence (anyonyāśraya, v.21) is blessed, not solved — the collection's frankest circle. Devotion is the only wealth that bursts all bonds.

essence: Feast announced: somehow-won sweetness, success dealings, all-state worship, touch-feasts, equinox tides, startless deeds, dreaming rulers, chanter grades, nectar-weddings, churn-born winnings (vv1-10).
